descriptionChirho: The basic Qal verbal action of judging, rendering a legal verdict, or administering justice — covering all finite Qal inflections (perfect, imperfect, imperative, consecutive, infinitive, infinitive absolute) where the sense is the general act of judicial decision-making; Arabic qada/hakama, Korean simpanhada/jaepanhada.

The Qal active participle used as a substantive noun designating a person who holds the office of judge (shofet/shoftim), including singular, plural, and construct forms with possessive suffixes; Arabic qadin/qudat, Korean jaepangwan, Swahili hakimu/mwamuzi.

Qal forms where judging carries a benefactive or vindicatory sense — judging on someone's behalf, defending the cause of the oppressed, or executing justice for a party; Arabic ihkum li (judge for me), Korean byeonhohada (to defend).

Niphal and related forms expressing reciprocal or intensive judicial action — entering into a lawsuit, contending at law, or litigating; Arabic haakama (form III, to litigate), mutahaakim (one contending), Korean sosong-hada (to litigate).

Niphal passive forms where the subject receives or undergoes judgment rather than administering it; Arabic yudaan (to be condemned), Swahili -hukumiwa (to be judged), Korean simpan-batda (to receive judgment).

Qal forms where shaphat extends beyond judicial decision to the broader sense of ruling, governing, or leading a people — characteristic of the Judges period; Arabic qada with governance connotation, Korean daseurida (to rule), Swahili -tawala (to govern).
